description:
Found by specled_-dn4.5 cold re-verification (2026-07-25T18:24:48Z, Note 1). Under bare 'mix spec.check' the tagged_tests verification leg intermittently red-lights on three tests — test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs:1452, :1681 and test/specled_ex/review_test.exs:135 — when the machine is loaded. All three passed on an immediate re-run and in isolation. Not attributable to dn4.5.

This is a THIRD flake class in this codebase's gate path, after specled_-ya8 (async code-server mutation, FIXED) and specled_-zr6 (StreamData generator space, open). Unlike zr6 it is load-sensitive rather than seed-sensitive, so it strikes exactly when the machine is busy — i.e. during parallel orchestration, which is when a red gate is most expensive.

Fix direction: serialize these three or widen their timing budget; commits c478563 (ya8) and d300c21 already hardened neighboring tests and are the pattern to follow.

Out of the dn4 epic (pre-existing; no gate blocked). If it red-lights two dn4 merge gates it should be escalated in like ya8 was.

New data point for this flaky class, observed 2026-07-25 while working specled_-cz0 on branch specled_-cz0/spec-honesty.

`mix spec.check` failed once in five runs, same session, no edits between runs:

  validate status=fail errors=1 warnings=0
  [ERROR] specled.package verification_command_failed .spec/specs/package.spec.md ::
    Verification command failed: tagged_tests: mix test --include integration ...
  failing tests: test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255
  spec.check result=fail tier=validate error_findings=1

Adds a file to this ticket's list, which so far names verifier_test.exs:1452/:1681 and review_test.exs:135.

What did NOT reproduce it (all green, exit 0):
  - mix test (full, no --include) x3
  - mix test --include integration (full suite)
  - mix test --include integration test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs (isolated)
  - mix spec.check x4 (the other four of the five)

Detail worth noting for whoever picks this up: line 255 is not a test declaration in that file. The tests bracket it at 250 ("a fabricated, unmarked finding code IS flagged") and 256/257 ("the evidence/* and cross_field/* families are guarded in both directions"); 255 is blank. Whatever emits the `failing tests:` line is reporting a line that does not correspond to a test declaration, which may be a lead on the reporting path rather than on the tests themselves.

Mechanism ruled out: a cwd race against the lint's relative corpus globs (`.spec/**/*.md`, `docs/**/*.md`). The only three File.cd! sites in the suite — binding_test.exs, coverage_closure_test.exs, spec_check_test.exs — are all async: false and carry comments saying exactly why, and ExUnit does not overlap sync modules with async ones.

The two tests bracketing line 255 are pure-constant assertions with no filesystem or process access, so neither can be load-sensitive on its own.

The bounce is on scope acceptance. Two of the four touched files — test/specled_ex/evidence/sync_test.exs:7 and test/specled_ex/coverage/aggregate_test.exs:14 — contain none of the three named tests, have never been observed flaking on this ticket or on ya8/zr6, and fall outside the ticket's fix direction ("serialize these three or widen their timing budget"). The VERIFY: PASS found this itself and wrote it down accurately ("the preemptive half of the scope expansion is evidence-free"; "a test in those modules regressing from 2.6s to 90s would now pass silently") and then admitted it as advisory. Three problems with that call:

1. The stated authorization is circular. VERIFY cites the TEST_CRITIC: FIXED comment of 2026-07-26T11:10:31Z as authorizing the expansion, but that comment is the resolution record describing the expansion, not a finding requiring it. The critic's BLOCKING finding was against the global raise in test_helper.exs; the minimal remedy for that finding is scoping the deadline to the two modules the ticket names. The two extra modules are an addition on top of the remedy, and nothing in the readable trail establishes that the critic prescribed four rather than the implementer choosing four. "Strictly narrower than the global raise it replaced" measures against the rejected d032ff0, not against base c13d1bd; against base, 19 tests lose runaway-regression sensitivity on no evidence.

2. The sole in-file justification for one of the two expansions is a figure the verifier itself measured as wrong. evidence/sync_test.exs:4 says "slowest test ~5s idle"; VERIFY measured 2.64s and filed it as a Note ("nothing rides on it"). Something does ride on it — that figure is the only evidence offered in the tree for why a module outside the ticket's scope needs 2-minute headroom, so a 2x overstatement is load-bearing for the scope decision, not cosmetic.

3. The standard is inconsistent across the two passes. Against d032ff0 the verifier treated a wrong wall-time figure in a comment ("Each such test's wall time equals this budget", actually 2x at five of seven sites) as a blocking Gap. Against 25f9a5f it treated the same class of defect — a wrong wall-time figure in a comment — as a Note, and the second one carries more weight than the first because it justifies out-of-contract scope rather than documenting an in-scope trade.

Bounce reason: Re-decide the scope call on test/specled_ex/evidence/sync_test.exs and test/specled_ex/coverage/aggregate_test.exs rather than recording it. Either (a) produce affirmative evidence that these two modules belong to this ticket's flake class — an observed red-light, or a stated rule the ticket's contract supports — or (b) raise the expansion to a Gap and route to the implementer to drop those two hunks, leaving the deadline on the two modules the ticket names. Also promote the evidence/sync_test.exs:4 "~5s idle" figure from Note to Gap for the same reason it was a Gap last pass, and re-measure rather than copy forward: the PASS carries stale line numbers from the d032ff0 pass — the three deliberately-left literals it cites at :1042/:1093/:1369 are at verifier_test.exs:1060/1111/1387 at 25f9a5f (shifted by the 18 lines added at the file head), and the budget attribute it places at :20 is at :21. Substance holds in each case, but the re-verification was partly copy-forward, which is what let the two judgment calls above through unre-examined.

On the lead's explicit question — yes, the narrower tag is strictly better, and it is nearly free: only VerifierTest, ReviewTest, Evidence.SyncTest, TracerIncrementalMergeTest, and Coverage.AggregateTest contain any test over 1.5s, so keeping 60s across the other ~1200 tests costs nothing and preserves the signal."

So the four-module choice was the critic's prescription (minus Tracer, which self-manages with 5-minute per-test tags), not silent implementer expansion. That answers provenance — but it does not answer the auditor's substantive point: a critic's nearly-free suggestion is not affirmative evidence that Evidence.SyncTest or Coverage.AggregateTest belong to this ticket's observed flake class, and neither module has ever red-lighted a gate.

Decision: adopt the auditor's option (b). The two preemptive hunks will be dropped, leaving the 2-minute deadline on exactly the two modules the ticket names (VerifierTest, ReviewTest). This also removes the evidence/sync_test.exs "~5s idle" figure the verifier measured at 2.64s, mooting the Gap-promotion request. If either module ever red-lights under load, that observation is a one-line follow-up with actual evidence behind it.
